banner_reopen_close_timer.cause: A decision in SlimStat's own banner adds the class that hides it at once and schedules the real close (the hidden attribute) 350 ms later. The "Privacy settings" link reopened the banner, and the scheduled close then shut it again. In the CI trace the link was clicked about 160 ms after Accept; the Decline click then waited on a hidden button until the 45 s timeout. The page snapshot at the timeout shows the banner closed. The test checks that the banner is hidden before it reopens it; that check passes as soon as the class is applied, so whether the reopen fell inside the 350 ms depended on how fast the first tracked request returned. The close timer and the reopen link both came in with 828b33da on this branch. 8141890e did not change this code.

findings.withdrawal: Fixed. Complianz, CookieYes and Real Cookie Banner report a withdrawal only through the WP Consent API change event. The tracker ignored a deny on that event, so the HttpOnly slimstat_tracking_code cookie stayed in the browser until it expired. A deny that follows full consent on the same page now reaches the consent endpoint, which deletes the cookie. A deny with no earlier consent sends nothing.

leftover_tracking_cookie.cause: The tracker cannot read the HttpOnly slimstat_tracking_code cookie, so it reports a withdrawal only when it saw full consent on the same page. Consent withdrawn where the tracker did not see it (another tab, a decision that expired, a page where the tracker did not run) left the cookie in the browser until it expired. The cookie was ignored while consent was denied. Separately, one browser test changed active_plugins before its try block, so a failing setup step could leave the site without its banner plugin.
leftover_tracking_cookie.fix: Session::deleteTrackingCookieWithoutConsent() runs on template_redirect at priority 1 on every front-end page request, tracked or not: when the cookie arrives and Consent::piiAllowed() is false, the cookie is expired. The tracker is unchanged: a page that starts without consent still sends no request. The comment at the withdrawal condition in wp-slimstat.js is corrected (the minified tracker is byte-identical; only the source map changed). The test setup moved into useWpConsentApiAlone(), called inside try.

limits: A page served from a full-page cache does not reach PHP. There the cookie stays until it expires (session_duration, 30 minutes by default) and is ignored while consent is denied.
template_redirect does not run for wp-admin, admin-ajax or REST requests; the cookie is removed by the next front-end page request.

wp_slimstat::slimtrack_server() bypasses consent by design and can set the cookie on a browser without consent. With GDPR mode on, anonymous tracking off and the tracker cookie on, that visitor's next front-end page request now removes the cookie, so later programmatic hits start a new visit.

Not counted as a result: the first real-banner run on this code failed at its first step for the three banner plugins because the test database had been restored and their setup was gone (logs in leftover-fix-no-banner-setup/). The setup was re-applied and the run repeated.

Real Cookie Banner: when a visitor leaves the page within a few tens of milliseconds of clicking 'Continue without consent', the banner does not store that decision. A later 'Accept all' from the privacy settings link stores consent, but Real Cookie Banner did not run the service's opt-in code on that page or the next one, so wp_consent_statistics stayed 'deny' and SlimStat did not track that visitor (it fails closed). Seen only in the test. The cause inside Real Cookie Banner was not investigated and later pages were not followed.
The Complianz, CookieYes, own-banner and with-Pro logs on 8141890e were made before the wait was added to the scenario file. The change only adds a wait; those runs were not repeated with it.
